proposals.before: Yuwen Huaji was the son of Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Yiwu Guard.
proposals.after: Yuwen Huaji was the son of Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Yiwei Guard.
proposals.reason: 左翊衞 is the Left Yiwei (wing) Guard; “Yiwu” is a mistranscription of 翊衞/Yiwei.

proposals.before: He sent Linghu Xingda to murder the emperor in the palace, seized dozens of courtiers who opposed him along with numerous imperial affines, and slaughtered them without regard to age, sparing only Prince Hao, son of Emperor Xiaojing of Qin, whom he enthroned as puppet emperor.
proposals.after: He sent Linghu Xingda to murder the emperor in the palace, seized dozens of courtiers who opposed him along with numerous imperial affines, and slaughtered them without regard to age, sparing only Prince Hao, son of Prince Xiao of Qin, whom he enthroned as puppet emperor.
proposals.reason: 秦孝王 is Prince Xiao of Qin, a princely not imperial title; “Emperor Xiaojing” misreads 孝王.

proposals.before: He sent Linghu Xingda to assassinate the emperor within the palace; he also seized several tens of court ministers who did not agree with him and various imperial affines, killing them without regard to age, sparing only Prince Hao, son of Emperor Xiaojing of Qin, whom he set up as emperor.
proposals.after: He sent Linghu Xingda to assassinate the emperor within the palace; he also seized several tens of court ministers who did not agree with him and various imperial affines, killing them without regard to age, sparing only Prince Hao, son of Prince Xiao of Qin, whom he set up as emperor.
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic line: 秦孝王 names Prince Xiao of Qin, not an emperor.

proposals.before: Yuwen Huaji—Yuwen Huaji was the son of Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Yiwu Guard.
proposals.after: Yuwen Huaji was the son of Yuwen Shu, General-in-Chief of the Left Yiwei Guard.
proposals.reason: Literal doubles the name and inherits the Yiwu/Yiwei error for 左翊衞.

proposals.before: Li Mi sent Xu Jixing to hold the Liyang granary.
proposals.after: Li Mi sent Xu Ji to hold the Liyang granary.
proposals.reason: Chinese 徐勣 is Xu Ji (later Li Ji); Jixing is a mistranslation of 勣.

proposals.before: Li Mi sent Xu Jixing to hold Liyang granary.
proposals.after: Li Mi sent Xu Ji to hold Liyang granary.
proposals.reason: Chinese 徐勣 is Xu Ji, not Xu Jixing.

proposals.before: Huaji was carted to Hejian, charged repeatedly with regicide, and beheaded with his sons Chenggi and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to the Turkic Princess Yicheng and displayed on the frontier.
proposals.after: Huaji was carted to Hejian, charged repeatedly with regicide, and beheaded with his sons Chengji and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to the Turkic Princess Yicheng and displayed on the frontier.
proposals.reason: 承基 is Chengji, not Chenggi.

proposals.before: Then they loaded Huaji on a caged cart to Hejian, repeatedly charged him with the crime of killing his sovereign, and beheaded him together with his two sons Chenggi and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to Princess Yicheng of the Turks and displayed in the barbarian court.
proposals.after: Then they loaded Huaji on a caged cart to Hejian, repeatedly charged him with the crime of killing his sovereign, and beheaded him together with his two sons Chengji and Chengzhi; their heads were sent to Princess Yicheng of the Turks and displayed in the barbarian court.
proposals.reason: 承基 is Chengji, not Chenggi.

proposals.before: In Daye year three he became hawk-raising gentleman.
proposals.after: In Daye year three he became Eagle-soaring Gentleman.
proposals.reason: 鷹揚郎將 is the Sui military office Yingyang langjiang, not a hawk-raising post.

proposals.before: In the third year of Daye he became Hawk-raising Gentleman.
proposals.after: In the third year of Daye he became Eagle-soaring Gentleman.
proposals.reason: 鷹揚郎將 is Yingyang langjiang, not hawk-raising.

proposals.before: Sima Dekan—Sima Dekan was a man of Yong in Fufeng.
proposals.after: Sima Dekan was a man of Yong in Fufeng.
proposals.reason: The literal line repeats the name after an em dash without adding meaning.

proposals.before: At Jiangdu he commanded ten thousand elite personal guards within the city.
proposals.after: Following the emperor to Jiangdu, he commanded ten thousand elite personal guards encamped within the city.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 從至江都 states that he followed to Jiangdu; the idiomatic sentence drops that motion and the encampment 營於城內.

proposals.before: At Xuzhou they disembarked; Huaji put Dekan in the rear guard while he plotted with Zhao Xingshu, Li Ben, Yin Zhengqing, Yuwen Daoshi, and others to strike Huaji and sent envoys to Meng Haigong for aid.
proposals.after: At Xuzhou they disembarked; Huaji ordered Dekan to command the rear guard, and Dekan with Zhao Xingshu, Li Ben, Yin Zhengqing, Yuwen Daoshi, and others plotted to surprise Huaji, sending men to Meng Haigong to ally as external aid.
proposals.reason: After 令德戡將後軍 the silent subject of 乃與…謀襲化及 is Dekan, not Huaji; the idiomatic he after naming Huaji reverses the conspirator.

proposals.before: On accession he promoted old intimates, making Qiantong Xuanhui captain then direct gate attendant.
proposals.after: On accession he promoted old intimates, appointing Qiantong as Xuanhui captain then transferring him to direct gate attendant.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line fuses the personal name Qiantong with the office 宣惠尉 as if Qiantong Xuanhui were a single name.

proposals.before: Shichong's father was raised by Can after the remarriage; Shichong took the Wang surname and his father became prefect of Huai and Bian.
proposals.after: His father, a young orphan, followed his mother when she married Can; Can loved and raised him, so he took the Wang surname and rose to chief administrator of Huai and Bian.
proposals.reason: 因姓王氏 and 官至懷、汴二州長史 continue the father's career, not Wang Shichong's; the idiomatic sentence assigns the surname change to Shichong and calls 長史 a prefect.

proposals.before: Shichong's father took in the young orphan; following his mother's remarriage to Can, Can loved and raised him, and therefore he took the surname Wang, rising to prefect of Huai and Bian prefectures.
proposals.after: His father, received as a young orphan, followed his mother when she married Can; Can loved and raised him, and therefore he took the surname Wang, rising to chief administrator of Huai and Bian prefectures.
proposals.reason: 其父收幼孤 is the father himself as the young orphan taken in, not a third person he adopted; 長史 is chief administrator, not prefect.

proposals.before: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Fen of Wu and Guan Chong of Jingling raised a hundred thousand in Jiangnan.
proposals.after: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Xie of Wu and Guan Chong of Jingling raised a hundred thousand in Jiangnan.
proposals.reason: The given name 爕 is Xie, not Fen; the English spelling invents a different personal name.

proposals.before: Following Wendu and Lu Chu's plan, Tong appointed Li Mi grand marshal; Mi submitted, fought Huaji at Liyang, and reported victory.
proposals.after: Following Wendu and Lu Chu's plan, Tong appointed Li Mi grand marshal and secretariat director; Mi submitted, fought Huaji at Liyang, and reported victory.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits 尚書令, which both the Chinese and the literal translation include.

proposals.before: The day was set until Duan Da's son-in-law Zhang Zhi exposed Chu's plot.
proposals.after: The appointed day had arrived when Duan Da's son-in-law Zhang Zhi reported Chu's plot.
proposals.reason: Until misreads 期有日矣: the ambush day was already fixed, not postponed until Zhang Zhi spoke.

proposals.before: Soon Shichong had Wei Jie urge Tong to name him left vice minister and supreme commander.
proposals.after: Soon Shichong had Wei Jie urge Tong to name him left vice director of the department of state affairs and commander of all internal and external military affairs.
proposals.reason: 尚書左僕射 is not left vice minister; that rendering names the wrong office.

proposals.before: Brother Wei and son Xuanying, prisoners of Mi since following Huaji, were recovered.
proposals.after: Shichong's elder brother Wei and his son Xuanying, who had followed Huaji to Dong commandery and been imprisoned by Mi, were all recovered.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence drops 充 and 東郡, hiding whose kin they are and where they were held.

proposals.before: He seized kin of Mi's officers, comforted them, and had them summon their men.
proposals.after: He also seized the wives and children of Mi's chief clerk Bing Yuanzhen, the mother of aide-de-camp Zheng Qianxiang, and the sons and younger brothers of various generals, comforted them, and had each secretly call their fathers and elder brothers.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic version erases named relatives and renders 邴 as Xing.

proposals.before: Duan Da—Duan Da was a man of Guzang in Wuwei.
proposals.after: Duan Da was a man of Guzang in Wuwei.
proposals.reason: The literal line duplicates the name in a false lemma split.

proposals.before: He pacified Fang and Chu in Gao Zhihui's rebellion, received a thousand bolts of silk, and rose to honored companion.
proposals.after: When Gao Zhihui, Li Ji, and others rebelled, Da led ten thousand men, pacified Dingfang and Chu prefectures, received a thousand bolts of silk, and was promoted to honored companion.
proposals.reason: 定方 is Dingfang, not Fang, and Li Ji plus the force of ten thousand are omitted.

proposals.before: He was soon restored as general of the Left Yiwu Guard.
proposals.after: He was soon restored as general of the Left Yiwei Guard.
proposals.reason: 翊衞 is Yiwei, not Yiwu; the office is Left Yiwei Guard.

proposals.before: Before long he was again appointed General of the Left Yiwu Guard.
proposals.after: Before long he was again appointed General of the Left Yiwei Guard.
proposals.reason: 翊衞 is Yiwei, not Yiwu; the office is Left Yiwei Guard.

proposals.before: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Wendu enthroned Prince Yue Tong, made him opening-the-government honored companion, chief speaker, and Duke of Chen.
proposals.after: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Wendu and others installed Prince Yue Tong as ruler; Da was appointed opening-the-government honored companion, concurrently chief speaker, and enfeoffed Duke of Chen.
proposals.reason: 署開府儀同三司兼納言封陳國公 are Da offices after installing Tong, not titles given to Tong.

proposals.before: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Yuan Wendu and others installed Prince Yue Tong as ruler, appointed him Opening the Government with Honored Companion of the Third Rank, concurrently Chief Speaker, and enfeoffed him Duke of Chen.
proposals.after: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Yuan Wendu and others installed Prince Yue Tong as ruler; Da was appointed Opening the Government with Honored Companion of the Third Rank, concurrently Chief Speaker, and enfeoffed Duke of Chen.
proposals.reason: The silent subject of 署 and 封 is Da, the biography subject, not Prince Yue Tong.

decisions.reason: 左翊衞 names the Left Yiwei Guard; Yiwu is a mistranscription of 翊衞.
秦孝王 is the princely title Prince Xiao of Qin, not an emperor named Xiaojing.
The same 秦孝王 phrase is princely, so Emperor Xiaojing of Qin is a mistranslation in the literal line as well.
The Chinese names 宇文化及 once, and 左翊衞 is Yiwei, not Yiwu; the doubled lemma and guard name are both errors.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宇文化及，左翊衞大將軍述之子也。

decisions.reason: 徐勣 is Xu Ji; Jixing is not a reading of 勣.
The literal line repeats the same false given name for 徐勣.
承基 is Chengji; Chenggi invents a different spelling of the same characters.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 并二子承基、承趾皆斬之

decisions.reason: The literal line has the same Chenggi error for 承基.
鷹揚郎將 is the Sui Yingyang command, an eagle-soaring military office, not a hawk-raising post.
The literal Hawk-raising Gentleman repeats the same mistranslation of 鷹揚.
司馬德戡 appears once before 扶風雍人也; the em-dash name doubling is not in the Chinese.
從至江都 records that he followed to Jiangdu, and 營於城內 that the ten thousand guards were encamped inside the city; both are missing from the original idiomatic line.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 從至江都，領左右備身驍果萬人，營於城內。

decisions.reason: After 令德戡將後軍, the silent subject of 乃與…謀襲化及 is Dekan; the original he after Huaji makes Huaji plot against himself.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 令德戡將後軍，乃與趙行樞、李本、尹正卿、宇文導師等謀襲化及

decisions.reason: 授宣惠尉 names the office Xuanhui captain; Qiantong Xuanhui wrongly fuses the person with the title.
因姓王氏 and 官至懷、汴二州長史 continue the career of 其父, the orphan raised by Can, not Shichong; 長史 is chief administrator, not prefect.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其父收幼孤，隨母嫁粲，粲愛而養之，因姓王氏，官至懷、汴二州長史。

decisions.after: His father, orphaned young, followed his mother when she married Can; Can loved and raised him, and therefore he took the surname Wang, rising to chief administrator of Huai and Bian prefectures.
decisions.reason: 其父 is himself the young orphan raised by Can, not an adopter of a third child, and 長史 is chief administrator; “received as a young orphan” is an awkward rendering of 收幼孤.

decisions.after: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Xie of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinling raised troops in Jiangnan in response, styled themselves generals, and mustered more than a hundred thousand.
decisions.reason: 爕 is Xie, not Fen, but the proposed line still writes Jingling for 晉陵 and drops 起兵…以應之, 自稱將軍, and 十餘萬.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 吳人朱爕、晉陵人管崇起兵江南以應之，自稱將軍，擁眾十餘萬

decisions.reason: 拜李密為太尉、尚書令 confers both Grand Marshal and Secretariat Director; the original idiomatic line omits 尚書令.

decisions.after: The day had already been set when General Duan Da sent his son-in-law Zhang Zhi to report Chu's plot.
decisions.reason: 期有日矣 means a date was already fixed, not that action waited until Zhang Zhi spoke; the proposal’s “had arrived” overreads 有日矣 and still drops 將軍段達遣.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 期有日矣，將軍段達遣其女婿張志以楚謀告之。

decisions.reason: 尚書左僕射 is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and 總督內外諸軍事 is command of inner and outer armies, not a vague supreme commander.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尚書左僕射、總督內外諸軍事

decisions.reason: 充兄偉及子玄應隨化及至東郡 identifies Shichong’s elder brother and son and the Dong commandery captivity omitted in the original.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 初，充兄偉及子玄應隨化及至東郡，密得而囚之於城中

decisions.reason: 邴元真 is Bing Yuanzhen, not Xing, and the line names his wives and children, Zheng Qianxiang’s mother, and the generals’ sons and younger brothers.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又執密長史邴元真妻子、司馬鄭虔象之母及諸將子弟

decisions.reason: 段達 appears once in 段達，武威姑臧人也; the doubled lemma is not in the Chinese.
The rebels are 高智惠、李積等, Da led 眾一萬, and the prefectures are 定方、滁, not Fang and Chu alone.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 高智惠、李積等之作亂也，達率眾一萬，擊定方、滁二州

decisions.reason: 左翊衞將軍 is General of the Left Yiwei Guard; Yiwu mistranscribes 翊衞.
The literal line has the same Yiwu error for 左翊衞將軍.
After 推越王侗為主, 署開府儀同三司，兼納言，封陳國公 are Da’s offices and enfeoffment, not titles given to Tong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 達與元文都等推越王侗為主，署開府儀同三司，兼納言，封陳國公。

decisions.reason: The silent subject of 署 and 封 is Da, the biography subject, not Prince Yue Tong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 署開府儀同三司，兼納言，封陳國公

claimRetractions.reason: Xing Yuanzhen is only the mistranslation of 邴元真 as Xing; the source supports Bing Yuanzhen, already claimed as c0485.

claimRevisions.reason: 秦孝王 is a princely title; the extracted English Emperor Xiaojing of Qin was produced only by the bad translation.
The English personal name Xu Jixing is unsupported; 徐勣 is Xu Ji.
The English form Chenggi is a mistranscription of 承基, whose pinyin is Chengji.
hawk-raising gentleman is the rejected calque of 鷹揚郎將; the office remains, with the English label aligned to the accepted repair.
Zhu Fen is an invented English given name for 爕, whose reading is Xie.
晉陵 is Jinling, not Jingling; the revised English of s0193 restores that native place.

value.action: with Zhu Fen raised troops in Jiangnan in response to Yang Xuangan
with Zhu Xie raised troops in Jiangnan in response to Yang Xuangan

claimRevisions.reason: The event remains, but the co-leader’s English name must follow 朱爕 as Zhu Xie.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 吳人朱爕、晉陵人管崇起兵江南以應之

sourceDate.text: 高智惠、李積等之作亂也
高智惠、李積等之作亂也

claimRevisions.reason: 擊定方、滁二州 names Dingfang and Chu, not Fang and Chu; the campaign fact stands with the place label corrected.
